documents.how_used:
HHSC says the Chapter 558 regulations dictate the required policies and that HHSC does not maintain a list of required HCSSA policies.
 I therefore used the rule sections that list written policies. §558.404 is the PAS-category section, and §558.521(d)(3) requires all policies to be available at the initial survey.

required_items.text: When developing its operational policies, the agency must make them considerate of individual and family choice and control, functional need, and accessible and flexible services.

Written policy, adopted, implemented and enforced, on health-related tasks done by unlicensed personnel that an RN may delegate or determines do not need delegation, in compliance with 22 TAC Chapter 225.

Written policy, in addition to the §558.245 staffing policies, addressing supervision of personnel with input from the client or family on the frequency of supervision.
 Supervisor qualifications are in §558.404(g)(2). Under §558.404(g)(1), supervision must follow agency policy, state law and 22 TAC Chapter 225.
Written staffing policies that govern all personnel used by the agency, including employees, volunteers, and contractors.
Requirements for orientation to the policies, procedures, and objectives of the agency.

Requirements for participation by all personnel in job-specific training. Training policies must ensure personnel are oriented to tasks and show competency when it cannot be determined through education, license, certification or experience (b)(2)(A)-(B). They must also ensure a continuing systematic training program (b)(2)(C).
Address participation by all personnel in appropriate employee development programs.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.245(b) (sub-paragraph number not verified; wording from HHSC CBT Module 2)

required_items.text: Include a written job description and job qualifications for each position at the agency.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.245(b) (sub-paragraph number not verified; wording from HHSC CBT Module 2)

required_items.text: Include procedures for processing criminal history checks and searches of the nurse aide registry and the employee misconduct registry for unlicensed personnel (see §558.247).
Ensure annual evaluation of employee and volunteer performance.
Address employee and volunteer disciplinary action and procedures.
Address use of volunteers, if volunteers are used (see §558.248).

Include a requirement that all direct care staff and staff with direct client contact, whether employed or contracted, sign a statement that they have read, understand and will comply with all applicable agency policies.
The license holder must adopt, implement, enforce and monitor agency policies required by Chapter 558.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.241 (summary from industry training handout; confirm in the rule text)

required_items.text: Written policy on the agency's procedures for investigating complaints and reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.243 (summary from industry training handout; confirm in the rule text)

required_items.text: Written policy on procedures for reporting alleged acts of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of a client by an employee of the agency.
Written policy on the agency's procedures for investigating complaints and reports of abuse, neglect, and exploitation. The policy must meet the requirements of §558.250.
Written policy ensuring all professional disciplines comply with their practice acts or title acts on reporting and peer review.

Written policy describing whether the agency conducts drug testing (disclosure of drug testing policy).
 The cited source text is truncated; confirm the wording in the rule.
Written policy ensuring the agency submits accurate billings and insurance claims.
Written policy ensuring compliance with Texas Occupations Code Chapter 102 on solicitation of patients.

A written emergency preparedness and response plan based on a risk assessment.
 
The plan must be reviewed internally at least annually and after each actual emergency response, and its response phase tested in a planned drill if not tested in an actual emergency.

Initial assessment, reassessment.
 Elements (1)-(16) of the client care policy are required only if covered under the agency's scope of services.
Start of care, placing services on hold, transfer, and discharge.
Intravenous services.
Care of the pediatric client.
Triaging clients in the event of disaster.
How to handle emergencies in the home.
Safety of staff.
Procedures the staff will perform for clients, such as dressing changes, Foley catheter changes, wound irrigation, administration of medication.
Psychiatric nursing procedures.
Patient and caregiver teaching relating to disease process/procedures.
Care planning.
Care of a client who has a terminal illness or a terminal prognosis.
Receiving physician orders.
Performing waived testing.
Medication monitoring.
Anything else pertaining to client care.

Written policy governing client conduct and responsibility and client rights, including a grievance mechanism under which a client can participate without fear of reprisal.
 
Before care begins, or at the initial evaluation visit, the client or legal representative must receive written notice of all these policies (§558.282(e)).

Written policy on implementing advance directives, in compliance with Health and Safety Code Chapter 166. It must clearly state any procedure the agency is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold.
 
Clients must be given written notice of the policy.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.283 (summary from industry training handout; confirm in the rule text)

required_items.text:
Written infection control policies, including preventing the spread of infectious and communicable disease. They must ensure compliance with Health and Safety Code Chapter 81, the OSHA bloodborne pathogens rule, and Health and Safety Code Chapter 85, Subchapter I.
 
They must require documentation of infections a client acquires while receiving services.

Written policy ensuring backup services are available when an employee or contractor is not available to deliver services. The only text I found for this section is HHSC's description of its proposed amendment. 
The proposal clarifies the written-policy requirement for ensuring backup services.
 Confirm the current text.
Written policy describing the agency's contingency plan, to be implemented on dissolution to assure continuity of client care. It must be consistent with §558.295 and comply with §558.217.
Written policy establishing time frame(s) for the initiation of care.
Written procedures on the use and removal of records, the release of information, and, when applicable, incorporating notes into the client record.
Written policy on retention of records; original client records must be kept at least five years after discharge.

sections: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services

notes: Texas has no policy checklist form for HCSSA-PAS. HHSC's FAQ says Chapter 558 dictates the required policies and that HHSC keeps no list. Policies are not submitted with the Form 2021 application. They are reviewed on-site at the initial survey: within 6 months of licensure the agency must admit at least one client and submit Form 2020 (Notification of Readiness for Initial Survey). At the survey the agency must have all agency policies required by Chapter 558, client records and personnel records ready for the surveyor (§558.521(a)-(d)). Organize the manual to follow the rule order above: Division 3 administration and staffing, Division 4 client care, rights and records, then PAS-specific §558.404, with section numbers cited in each policy so a surveyor can match policy to rule. For PAS, §558.281 elements apply only if within the agency's scope of services. The 558.404(e) policy principles (individual and family choice and control, functional need, accessible and flexible services) apply to all operational policies. Also include a client-file template for the §558.404(f) individualized service plan, which must be signed by the client or family and the agency. §558.404(f)(2)(A)-(F) lists what it must contain. The 9/18/2026 Texas Register proposals would change §§558.245 (registry searches), 558.249, 558.250, 558.256, 558.281, 558.288 and 558.290. They also add a new §558.251 on reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation and a workplace-violence policy for agencies with 2+ nurses, which does not apply to PAS-only agencies. Re-check the TAC before finalizing. I could not retrieve the full current text of these sections, so check them directly against the rule: 558.243 (complaint/ANE procedures), 558.247 and 558.248 (employability checks, volunteers), 558.253, 558.287 (QAPI), 558.288 (coordination of services), 558.289 (contractors), 558.292 (agency-client agreement and disclosure), 558.295 (transfer/discharge notice) and 558.300 (medication administration). For the 558.245(b) elements beyond (b)(1)-(2), I took the wording from HHSC's CBT summary and could not verify the sub-paragraph numbers. Separate Medicaid contracting requirements (26 TAC Chapter 277 for PHC/CAS/FC, MCO credentialing, EVV) were not reviewed here.
